verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'really bad tummy egg... at the lower bottom of my belly', located in the middle, present 'all the time', started 'a few days ago' and 'is getting worse', and rates pain 'maybe 8' on a 1–10 scale.
Location and constancy are described: 'like lower. In my lower abdomen', 'No, it's in the middle', 'Below [the belly button]', and 'It's there all the time.'

Patient states 'I have like vaginal, sometime bleeding... it's like light color' and clarifies it is 'since your period stopped ... my period stopped like last two weeks ago ... it's just light pink color.'
In response to nausea/vomiting: 'Yeah, I feel nausea. Like, I feel like vomiting, but I don't. I get nauseated, but I don't vomit.'
Bowel history: 'Like I was constipated for a week... And what about this week? ... it seems to be okay. It's fine now.'
On urinary frequency: 'I don't really. I have noticed that I don't really go often like before. So, yeah, I do. I do drink a lot though.' This supports decreased urinary frequency.

Patient denies these symptoms: 'Any difficulty breathing or pain in your shoulders... ? No.'; 'Do you feel feverish? No.'; 'Do you feel faint when you stand up? No.'; 'Any chain, Any weight loss or blood in the stool or urine? ... Other than that, there is not discharge.' No weight loss or blood in stool/urine are implied by this question and lack of positive response.
Menstrual history: 'My last month? Two weeks ago. I'm sorry, about two weeks. Three weeks ago.' and 'And was your last period normal? Yeah.' This supports an LMP about 2–3 weeks ago and normal.

Cycle pattern on Implanon: 'Do you have your periods when you. Since you've been using the Implanon, do you have periods?' 'Yes...'; 'Or are they sporadic?' 'No, they are sporadic. Like not the time it changes.' This indicates irregular cycles.
Sexual activity: 'And are you having sexual intercourse regularly? Yes, Yes, I do.' and 'Four weeks ago. Four days ago. Sorry, I just had.' indicating last intercourse 4 days ago.

Transcript: 'Have you taken a pregnancy test this time?' 'Yeah, I did.' 'When was that?' 'Yeah, around like a month ago.' No result (positive or negative) is documented; stating it was negative adds information not in the transcript.
Past history: 'Yeah, I have allergy. I have Amy.' 'Pardon?' 'Ammo. Excellent allergy.' Although unclear, it matches a reported allergy described similarly.
Surgical history: 'Anything else? Have you had any operations?' 'No.'
Obstetric history: 'Have you had any pregnancies?' 'No.'

Contraception: 'Are you using any contraception?' 'Yes, I am. I use it from last one year. Plan on calling. Plan.' Doctor later: 'And your Implanon was just put in a year ago? Yes.' This supports Implanon use.
Occupation: 'And what's your job day to day?' 'Yeah, I'm a teacher.'
Living situation: 'And who do you live with at home?' 'My husband and my husband's family.'
Substance use: 'And do you smoke or drink alcohol? You take any other drugs?' 'No.'
Travel: 'Have you been abroad recently?' 'Yes.' 'Whereabouts to?' 'About a year.' 'Pardon? Oh, a year ago. Not recently? No.' This indicates travel abroad one year ago.

Assessment of worsening lower abdominal pain is consistent with history: 'really bad tummy egg... lower abdomen... It's there all the time... It is getting worse... been going on for the last few days.' Etiology is not specified, so 'to be determined' matches.
Post-menstrual light bleeding: 'my period stopped like last two weeks ago. And this is different... it's just light pink color.'
Nausea without vomiting as part of assessment matches: 'I feel nausea... I feel like vomiting, but I don't. I get nauseated, but I don't vomit.'
Resolved constipation: 'Like I was constipated for a week... And what about this week? ... it seems to be okay. It's fine now.'
Plan: 'we can arrange a face to face examination where they can see you in a clinic and do an abdominal examination... Would you be happy to call the support line and arrange that appointment?'
'The other thing we would need to do is to do a pregnancy test today if possible. So if you can do that today and if it's positive, we need to see you straight away. So give us a call back.'

Safety netting: 'In the meantime, if it gets a lot worse or you. You're not holding any fluids down, then we should see you before then.' This matches return sooner if pain intensifies or unable to tolerate oral fluids.
